data.exact_reserve_text:
This result has benefited from a substantial release of reserves from prior years of account now available due to the continuing favourable trends experienced during the last few years in incurred claims development on all years of account, despite the recent emergence of some new sources of claims in the liability book. The utilisation of the reserve for incurred but not reported claims has been, as it was last year, very light.

Within this profit, there was a profit arising from the reinsurance to close received from 2013 year of account of GBP 13.3m before expenses and investment return. This arose largely from a reduction in the 2013 and prior years' liability reserves as a result of favourable settlements in 2016.

With only two exceptions, the picture painted above is what should be expected with a conservative reserving policy. The first exception, the strengthening of the third party liability reserves during 2015, was a consequence of it becoming clear that changes to the policy wordings given to contractors were not producing the forecast ultimate loss ratios. The second exception, the strengthening of the liability reinsurance reserves during 2016 reflects the recent emergence of some new sources of claims in the liability book.

The profit on the General Business Technical Account for the calendar year 2016 is higher than that achieved in calendar year 2015 by GBP 7.2m, the increase being 11.1% of the net earned premium, largely because of releases from reserves on some of the Syndicate's older business.

data.standardized_narrative: At 31 December 2016 the Syndicate carried opening gross claims outstanding of GBP 245.893m. Using the gross claims development triangle, older underwriting years produced a net favourable development of approximately GBP 7.10m (a release of ~2.9% of opening reserves). The release was driven by favourable settlements and generally benign claims development on older years, partly offset by adverse developments arising from recent new sources of liability claims and some strengthening in liability reinsurance and third party liability reserves. The movement predominantly affected casualty/liability and property-related lines.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development was calculated from the gross claims development triangle (gross amounts in GBP '000) because no single explicit gross 'movement in prior year's provision' line was provided. The triangle excludes the '2010 and prior' aggregate column from calculations as required. Some LOB reserve movement figures presented in the notes are net of reinsurance; lob_movements therefore uses net figures where only net data was available (confidence 0.5). One regulatory premium line (Credit and suretyship) shows a negative gross premium in the note which is reproduced verbatim. Reinsurance-to-close entries for closed years are present elsewhere (affecting closed-year balances) but the triangle-based PYD avoids RITC distortion for the individual UW years used.
